## PART II: BRING-DOWN REPS & COVENANTS CERTIFICATION

### Section D — Bring-Down Diligence Summary

**Scope:** This bring-down covers the period from the Signing Date through the Closing Date and is intended to confirm that (i) Seller's representations and warranties remain true and correct as of the Closing Date with the same force and effect as if made on and as of the Closing Date (subject to applicable materiality qualifiers), and (ii) all pre-closing covenants have been complied with in all material respects.

| Rep # | Tax Representation Topic | Bring-Down Standard | Verified |

| TR-2 | All Taxes shown as due on filed returns have been paid in full or properly accrued | True and correct in all respects | ☐ |

> **TAX-PROV-6** — If any Tax Representation listed in D-1 cannot be certified as true and correct as of the Closing Date, Seller shall promptly notify Buyer's Tax Partner in writing, describe the nature and scope of the exception, and propose a remediation plan. Buyer, in its sole discretion, may (a) waive the applicable condition, (b) require an increase to the Tax Escrow Amount, (c) seek specific indemnification, or (d) decline to close if the exception constitutes a Material Adverse Effect.

## PART III: STRUCTURE SELECTION & ELECTIONS

### Section E — Transaction Structure Summary & Tax Elections

#### E-1 Structure Selection Analysis

> **TAX-PROV-9** — The Parties acknowledge that the Transaction is structured as [●] (e.g., stock purchase / merger / asset purchase) (the "Acquisition Structure"). The Parties' respective tax advisors have reviewed the following alternative structures and the Acquisition Structure has been selected based on the considerations described below:

| Structure | Seller Tax Cost | Buyer Tax Benefit | Net Economic Impact | Selected? |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------|---------------------|-----------|
| Stock Purchase (No Election) | Capital gains on stock sale | Carry-over basis; no step-up | Neutral to Seller; adverse to Buyer | — |
| Stock Purchase + § 338(h)(10) | Ordinary income on deemed asset sale (offset by higher price) | Full FMV step-up in assets; depreciation/amortization benefit | Price gross-up negotiated | ✓ |
| Stock Purchase + § 336(e) | Similar to § 338(h)(10) for S-corp/subsidiary | FMV step-up in assets | Consider if § 338(h)(10) unavailable | Backup |
| Asset Purchase | Ordinary income on hot assets; LIFO recapture | Step-up in all assets; full § 197 amortization | State tax complications | Alternative |
| Merger (Forward/Reverse Triangular) | Potential tax-free treatment if stock-for-stock | No step-up unless § 338 election | Applicable if rollover >50% | Alternative |

> **TAX-PROV-10** — If a Section 338(h)(10) election is made, Buyer and Seller shall jointly execute IRS Form 8023 no later than the fifteenth (15th) day of the ninth (9th) month following the month in which the Acquisition Date occurs. Buyer's Tax Partner shall prepare a draft Form 8023 within thirty (30) days after Closing for Seller's review and approval. Any disagreement regarding the election form shall be resolved pursuant to the dispute resolution mechanism in the Purchase Agreement.

#### E-2 Purchase Price Allocation

> **TAX-PROV-11** — The Purchase Price (as adjusted pursuant to the working capital and net debt adjustment mechanisms) shall be allocated among the acquired assets in accordance with IRC § 1060 and the residual method prescribed by Treas. Reg. § 1.1060-1. The allocation shall be prepared by Buyer's Tax Partner and delivered to Seller within ninety (90) days following final determination of the Closing Purchase Price. Seller shall have thirty (30) days to review and propose modifications. The agreed allocation (the "Allocation Schedule") shall be binding on all Parties for all Tax purposes, including all Tax Returns and IRS Forms 8594.

**Preliminary Allocation Framework (to be finalized):**

| Asset Class (IRC § 338 / § 1060) | Description | Preliminary Value |
|----------------------------------|-------------|------------------|
| Class I | Cash and cash equivalents | FMV |
| Class II | Actively traded personal property (securities) | FMV |
| Class III | Marked-to-market assets (accounts receivable) | FMV |
| Class IV | Inventory (if any) | FMV |
| Class V | Other tangible personal property; real property | Appraised FMV |
| Class VI | § 197 intangibles (other than goodwill) — customer lists, IP, non-competes | Appraised FMV |
| Class VII | Goodwill and going-concern value | Residual |

> **TAX-PROV-12** — Buyer and Seller shall each bear their own costs incurred in connection with any appraisal required to support the Allocation Schedule. To the extent an independent appraiser is jointly engaged, the cost shall be shared equally. Neither Party shall take any Tax Return position inconsistent with the Allocation Schedule without prior written consent of the other Party, except as required by a final determination within the meaning of IRC § 1313(a).

#### E-3 Rollover Equity Validation

> **TAX-PROV-13** — The rollover equity investment by Continuing Stockholders (as defined in the Rollover Agreement) has been structured to qualify as a tax-deferred contribution under IRC § 351 or as part of a tax-free reorganization (as applicable). Buyer's Tax Partner and Seller's Tax Counsel have reviewed the following metrics to confirm eligibility:

| Metric | Required Threshold | Validated Value | Status |
|--------|--------------------|-----------------|--------|
| Rollover percentage (rolled equity / total equity) | ≥ 20% (for § 351 control) or as required for reorganization | ___% | ☐ |
| FMV of rolled units at Closing (supported by 409A / independent valuation) | Per agreed Valuation | $_________ | ☐ |
| No "boot" received by Continuing Stockholders exceeding permissible threshold | ≤ agreed % | $_________ | ☐ |
| Holding period for long-term capital gain on earnout (if applicable) | > 1 year from original acquisition date | _____ | ☐ |
| § 704(c) / § 743(b) adjustments for partnership rollover (if applicable) | Documented in LLC Agreement | N/A / ☐ | ☐ |

> **TAX-PROV-14** — No Continuing Stockholder shall receive cash boot in connection with the rollover in excess of the "boot ceiling" set forth in the Rollover Agreement without the prior written consent of Buyer's Tax Partner. Excess boot shall cause a deemed taxable sale of the corresponding pro rata portion of the rolled equity, and Seller's Tax Counsel shall compute the resulting gain and prepare appropriate disclosure to be included in the Closing Tax Deliverables Package.

#### E-4 Earnout Tax Treatment

> **TAX-PROV-15** — Earnout payments, if any, shall be treated as additional purchase price for Tax purposes and characterized as capital gain (long-term or short-term, based on the applicable holding period) unless otherwise agreed in writing. Buyer shall not deduct earnout payments as compensation unless a payment has been specifically designated as compensatory in the Purchase Agreement and confirmed by Buyer's Tax Partner. The Parties shall consider whether the open transaction doctrine or installment sale method applies to earnout payments subject to contingency, and Buyer's Tax Partner shall deliver a written analysis (the "Earnout Tax Analysis") to both Parties within forty-five (45) days after Closing.

**Earnout EBITDA Metrics — Validation Summary:**

| Year 1 (FY2027) | $_________ | $_________ | $_________ | $_____ | ☐ Validated |
| Year 2 (FY2028) | $_________ | $_________ | $_________ | $_____ | ☐ Validated |
| Year 3 (FY2029) | $_________ | $_________ | $_________ | $_____ | ☐ Validated |

> **TAX-PROV-16** — The EBITDA calculation methodology for purposes of the earnout shall be the same as used in the Company's audited financial statements, adjusted for the exclusions and addbacks set forth in Exhibit [●] to the Purchase Agreement (the "Earnout Calculation Protocol"). Any post-closing change in accounting method, policy, or fiscal year that would materially affect the EBITDA calculation shall require the prior written consent of the Seller Representative and shall not be taken into account in computing Earnout Payments unless both Parties consent in writing.

> **TAX-PROV-19** — Buyer's Tax Partner shall commission a Section 382 study within ninety (90) days of the Closing Date to determine the annual § 382 limitation applicable to the Company's pre-acquisition net operating loss carryforwards. Seller shall cooperate fully and provide all historical equity ownership records, option exercise histories, and other information reasonably required to complete such study. The results of the § 382 study shall be incorporated into Buyer's post-closing Tax planning and shall be reflected in the first Tax Return filed by the Buyer group that includes the Company.

> **TAX-PROV-20** — All disputes between Buyer and Seller regarding (i) the preparation or filing of any Pre-Closing Period Tax Return, (ii) the Allocation Schedule, (iii) the Earnout EBITDA calculation methodology, or (iv) indemnification for Taxes shall be resolved by an independent accounting firm of national recognition mutually agreed upon by the Parties (the "Tax Arbitrator"). The Tax Arbitrator shall act as an expert and not as an arbitrator, and its determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The costs of the Tax Arbitrator shall be borne by the non-prevailing Party, or equally if neither Party substantially prevails.
